:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useVueDefaultExport`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/require-default-export`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/require-default-export)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueDefaultExport": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require the `<script>` block of a Vue component to have a default export.

When a `.vue` file has no `<script setup>` block, Vue builds the component from the
default export of its `<script>` block. If the block has no default export, the
component can't use anything the block declares, such as data, props, or methods.

A file with a `<script setup>` block is not checked, because Vue builds the component
from that block instead.

:::note
This rule needs to read every block of a `.vue` file, which requires
[`html.experimentalFullSupportEnabled`](https://biomejs.dev/reference/configuration/#htmlexperimentalfullsupportenabled)
to be `true`. Without that setting, the rule reports nothing.
:::

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<script>
const foo = "foo";
</script>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

```vue
<script>
import { defineComponent } from "vue";

export const component = defineComponent({});
</script>
```

<Fragment set:html={"<pre class=\"language-text\"><code class=\"language-text\"></code></pre>"} />

### Valid

```vue
<script>
export default {
  data() {
    return {
      foo: "foo",
    };
  },
};
</script>
```

```vue
<script>
export const foo = "foo";
</script>

<script setup>
const bar = "bar";
</script>
```
